context:
Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).

2026-11-20 evidence. BenchBox: generator_specs.yaml sets market_history 541550; scaling.py computes max(1, int(541550 x SF)); generator/facts.py writes that many rows with a random security and a random date, so the count is not derived from securities x days; source_generators.py uses the same constant. The constant is R_H 541.55 for DailyMarket.txt in Poess et al., PVLDB vol. 7 p. 1367, Table 3 (the design paper), not the specification; the #4171 commit message calls it the specification's factor. TPC-DI v1.1.0 gives no DailyMarket row count (clause 2.1: row counts are 'determined by the data generator based on the Scale Factor'). 584,800 = 731 x 800; the official generator's config (DIGen 1.1.0 tpc-di-schema.xml, read from a third-party copy) computes 732 calendar days x 0.8 x SF = 585,600 per unit and marks it 'FAKE VALUE.customBB overrides this'. So the site's 'two years of trading days' is wrong: calendar days, and a placeholder. UNVERIFIED: DIGen's real DailyMarket row count (needs running DIGen.jar under its EULA); an estimate from securities alive in 2015-2017 gives about 546,900 per unit, within 1% of 541,550. Owner questions, none preselected: (a) keep 541,550 and correct the site text; (b) run DIGen at SF 3 or 5 and adopt the measured factor; (c) generate one row per alive security per calendar day; (b) and (c) change TPC-DI data digests. May DIGen.jar be run in /tmp to measure?
description:
## Problem
tpcdi-remaining-spec-differences-20261112 requires an owner-approved rationale for each difference 'including 541550 versus 584800'. It was closed with that difference recorded as 'cause not investigated'. The site text on `next` gives the arithmetic as trading days although 584800 / 800 is 731 calendar days.

## Change
Find the cause in the generator and the specification clause; record the rationale; then either fix the generator or keep the difference with the owner's approval.

## Decision gates
Changing generated row counts changes TPC-DI data digests: owner approval before any generator change.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the item records the specification clause, the generator code path and the arithmetic for both numbers, and the owner's keep-or-fix decision.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
